fieldMarks: 21-25 in; small white goose, smaller than a Snow Goose.
Short bill lacking the Snow Goose's black 'grinning patch', often with a bumpy blue-gray base.
Rounder head with the eye more centered, giving a gentle expression.
Young are much whiter than young Snow Geese; a rare blue morph exists.
behavior: Migrates and winters in flocks, often mixed with Snow Geese; hybrids occur.
Feeds by walking, wading or swimming in shallow water; mainly green grasses and sedges, plus seeds and grain in fall.
Calls are soft cackling and grunting notes.
habitat: Summer on flat Arctic tundra mixing grass and low dwarf birch or willow.
Migration and winter on shallow lakes, freshwater marshes and flooded stubble and other farm fields.
range: Main population breeds in the central Canadian Arctic (Northwest Territories/Nunavut region) and migrates through Alberta and Montana to winter in central California; wintering numbers in New Mexico and east of the Rockies have increased markedly.

lookalikes.name: Snow goose
lookalikes.howToTell: Snow goose is larger with a longer bill showing a black 'grinning patch'; Ross's has a rounder head with a more centered eye.
